title: As a developer, I can deliver as-you-type instant search with millisecond responses so results update on every keystroke
As a developer, searches tolerate typos and misspellings out of the box, with tunable rules for when and how fuzzy matching applies
As a developer, I can build faceted navigation — filters with live counts across categories, ranges, and attributes — from a single query
As a developer, I can serve query suggestions and autocomplete backed by real search traffic or a suggestions index
As a developer, I can shape relevance with custom ranking rules and business signals (popularity, recency, margin) beyond textual matching
As a developer, I can define synonyms and curate results — pin, boost, or hide specific hits for specific queries
As a platform-engineer, I can inspect ranking scores or explanations to understand exactly why a result ranked where it did
As a developer, I can run hybrid search — semantic vector similarity fused with keyword matching — in a single query
As a developer, I can use built-in or managed embedders so documents and queries are vectorized without running my own embedding pipeline
As a developer, I can power RAG and conversational answers on top of my indexes with documented retrieval or answer APIs
As a platform-engineer, I can bulk-import millions of documents quickly, with async task tracking to know when indexing completes
As a developer, document adds, updates, and deletes become searchable in near real time without a full reindex
As a founder, I can ingest content with an official crawler or connectors instead of writing my own indexing pipeline
As a developer, I can create an index, add documents, and run my first search within minutes of starting the quickstart
As a developer, official SDKs cover my language and framework, kept current across JavaScript, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, and more
As a developer, official UI component libraries let me assemble a full search interface — box, results, facets, pagination — without building it from scratch
As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the full engine — same features as the hosted product — on my own infrastructure
As a founder, built-in analytics show top queries, no-result queries, and click-through so I know what users search for and miss
As a platform-engineer, documented scaling paths — clustering, replication, high availability — carry me from prototype to hundreds of millions of documents
As a developer, scoped or tenant tokens restrict each end user's searches to their own documents without separate indexes per user
As a founder, published per-unit pricing (searches, records, or nodes) lets me predict what search will cost before committing
As a founder, costs stay predictable as records and query volume grow — no surprise per-request cliffs
As an AI-native user, my coding agent can create an index, add documents, and run queries end to end — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching a dashboard
As an AI-native user, agents can use my search indexes as a tool — an MCP server or tool-calling surface exposes query, analytics, and index operations
